full_judgment:
K. Hossain, C. J:—the question involved in this appeal is whether the preemption petition filed under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act earlier to the registration of the sale deed under pre-emption is competent. The trial Court held that subsequent registration of the Kabala during the pendency of the application cured the prematurity which was reversed by the First Appellate Court and the High Court and the soundness of this decision is in question. As to the standing of the pre-emptor and the competency of his application on merit is not in question. The only question is the one that has been set out above. 

 2. The facts for consideration of this appeal are that the Kabala under preemption was executed on 26-7-72, it was presented for registration before the Sub-Registrar on 29-7-72 and was registered under section 60 of the Registration Act on 11-8-72. Three days earlier to the registration i.e., on 8-8-72 the application for pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was filed. It is to be observed that the Kabala under pre-emption was duly exhibited in the Court and the trial Court found that the registration made on 11-8-72 during the pendency of the proceeding had cured the defect of prematurity. The Court of appeal below as well as the High Court took the view that the day on which the application for pre-emption was presented in Court the deed was not registered and so the cause of act ion did not accrue. On this point the learned Single Judge relied on two decisions of the Dacca High Court in the case of Muhammad Maharani Mondale Vs. Muhammad Ali Sarkar, (1965) 17 DLR 365, and Abdur Rahman Vs. Baser Ali (1969) 21 DLR 99. in  heeded ions it has been held that the cause of action for preemption accrues on the date of the registration of the kabala where registration is compulsory. As a  of law, no exception can be taken to this view, but where the learned Judge fell it to an error is in holding that the pre-meturity of the cause of action, if, matured during the pendency of the 1rreceding is not curable. This view is untenable. The document itself was produced before the trial Court and before decision was given and so the matter we s brought on record as to the maturity of the cause of action and before the decision was given.
